ctx.x: Mm-hmm. Lots of musicians in. Lots of musicians. Who were some of the other ones that you... What were the other ones that you...

Well, uh... Milford Piron, my teacher. Armand Piron. Thank you. Louis Cottrell's daddy. Bonnie Bigard, the Teos. Lorenzo Junior, Lorenzo Senior. Big I, Louis. Well, we could just go on and name quite a number of them. Piku.
The guys your age, how many of them are there? Let's see.

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1961-05-11
items.q: The only real professor I had, like I said, was Mr. Piran.

ctx.x: Great man. I have over a hundred tapes about him. The complete story of his life. He's a great talker, a very slow talker. That's right. He has a wonderful memory and has played so many years. Started about 1907 or so playing professionally. And he gave up playing about 1922 or so. Did you ever study with him by any chance?
No, I never had to. I didn't study with him. You'd left. I had left New Orleans. The only real professor I had, like I said, was Mr. Piran.
Did he, on the trumpet itself, did you learn from Piran? Did he help you on the trumpet then?

Yeah, fine. And, well, from there, my daddy was a singer and a violin player. I couldn't stand the violin. I tried it, but that was out of question. So I took up singing, as I told you a lot of times in our interviews. And from there, I went to learn the horn, the music first, and then the horn from Milford Pierron, who was the brother of the violin player. And then after I learned from him how to blow the horn, I got pretty good, and I went to take a job with Bigfoot Phillips. And he told me I learned enough…
